themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 26 THIS WEEK—a 2,871% increase compared to the 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid deterioration of enforcement in East Flatbush.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 27.1)
2,871% spike represents most extreme statistical deviation in district data
Complaint volume 29x higher than baseline—far exceeding typical variance
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks to document visible graffiti and map pattern (tags from single crew or multiple?)
Interview NYPD/Sanitation about response protocol and resources deployed THIS WEEK

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints reached 52 THIS WEEK, a 320% increase from the 12.4 weekly average, indicating potential accelerating pavement damage, pothole formation, or infrastructure failure across the district.
evidence: 52 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.4 weekly average (z-score: 6.75)
320% spike sustained over single-week reporting window
318 active DOB permits (173 alterations + 85 new buildings) suggest ongoing construction that may be damaging streets
reporting_angles: Drive-and-document major potholes and pavement failures across priority blocks
Cross-reference spike timing with DOT repair schedules and recent construction projects

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK—a 2,300% spike from the 0.1 weekly average—raising concerns about aging wiring infrastructure or overloaded systems in residential buildings.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69)
2,300% increase represents extreme deviation from baseline
Coincides with sustained heat/hot water crisis (4,779 complaints over 90 days), suggesting possible grid strain
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison about service calls and outage patterns in CD 317 this week/last week
Report on age of building stock and electrical code compliance in affected blocks

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Cascade
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping, residential disposal, and commercial disposal complaints surged 2 WEEKS AGO—15 sweeping (UP 823%), 11 residential (UP 252%), and 4 commercial (UP 1,500%)—indicating systemic collection or street maintenance failures.
evidence: Street sweeping: 15 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.71, up 823%)
Residential disposal: 11 complaints vs. 3.1 average (z-score: 6.75, up 252%)
Commercial disposal: 4 complaints vs. 0.2 average (z-score: 5.67, up 1,500%)
Convergence of three sanitation vectors suggests fleet breakdown, staffing shortage, or route disruption
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about collection schedule disruptions and vehicle status 2 weeks ago
Canvass blocks to document overflowing baskets and unsanitary conditions

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Tree complaints spiked to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 1,300% increase from the 0.5 weekly average—suggesting environmental stress, disease, storm damage, or deferred maintenance across the district's canopy.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 9.19, up 1,300%)
Spike timing suggests possible weather-related trigger or pest outbreak
Follows consistent year-round heat/hot water complaints (4,779 over 90 days), indicating potential heat island effect
reporting_angles: Partner with NYC Parks to identify tree species at risk and disease vectors in CD 317
Report on canopy equity: compare tree density/health in East Flatbush vs. wealthier neighborhoods

land_use.brief: A UDAAP and disposition to facilitate a new four-story building, containing 12 residential units is being sought by HPD at 395 East 94th Street in the East Flatbush neighborhood of Brooklyn, Community
land_use.applicant: HPD - NYC Dept of Housing Preservation & Development
